summary: Arguments are the words you type after a script's name. Inside the script, $1 is the first, $2 the second, $# is how many there are, and $@ or $* is all of them.
notes: "the CS quiz" is in quotes, so it arrives as one argument ($2). Without quotes it would be three.
./shoutout.sh Ava Smith gives 2 arguments, so Smith becomes the event. "Ava Smith" in quotes is 1 argument.
$0 is the name you used to run the script, here ./shoutout.sh. shift with no arguments left does nothing.
pitfall: Forgetting quotes around an argument with spaces splits it. ./shoutout.sh Ava Smith prints Great job at Smith, Ava! because Smith became $2.
